pages.title: Ketonemia — Blood Ketone Signal Reference
pages.core_function: Category identity and reference map for blood ketone signal language.

pages.title: Definition of Ketonemia
pages.core_function: Defines ketonemia as a blood measurement state.

pages.title: Blood Ketones
pages.core_function: What a blood ketone measurement represents and what it cannot tell you alone.

pages.title: Beta-Hydroxybutyrate
pages.core_function: The primary blood ketone body: biochemistry, role, and measurement.

pages.title: Ketone Bodies
pages.core_function: The three ketone bodies (beta-hydroxybutyrate, acetoacetate, acetone): hepatic ketogenesis, interconversion, and the mapping of each compound to its measurement layer (blood/urine/breath). Ketone-body presence is not a diagnosis and does not equal ketoacidosis.

pages.title: Urine Ketones (Ketonuria)
pages.core_function: Urine ketone testing measures mostly acetoacetate (AcAc), not the beta-hydroxybutyrate measured in blood; it is time-lagged and semi-quantitative, and is not interchangeable with blood ketones.

pages.title: Breath Ketones (Breath Acetone)
pages.core_function: Breath ketone analyzers measure exhaled acetone as a proxy for ketone state, not the beta-hydroxybutyrate measured in blood; it is a non-invasive trend indicator, sensor-based, and not interchangeable with a blood ketone value.

pages.title: Ketonemia vs. Ketosis
pages.core_function: Distinguishes a blood measurement state from a metabolic state.

pages.title: Fasting Ketones
pages.core_function: Why blood ketones rise during fasting: falling glucose and insulin shift the liver to ketogenesis, raising BHB as fuel. An expected physiological rise whose meaning still depends on context (diabetes, medication, illness, pregnancy, prolonged fasting). Not equal to ketoacidosis; no numeric thresholds.

pages.title: Nutritional Ketosis
pages.core_function: Nutritional ketosis as a diet-driven metabolic state of sustained ketone-body elevation from a low-carbohydrate diet; related to but not identical with ketonemia (the measurement), and distinct from fasting ketosis and from ketoacidosis. No numeric thresholds, no diet advice, no health claims.

pages.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors and Blood Ketones
pages.core_function: How SGLT2-inhibitor medication changes the interpretation of a blood ketone signal: regulator-warned ketoacidosis risk that can occur without markedly elevated glucose, so normal glucose does not by itself rule out concern. Reference only; no medication advice, dosing, diagnosis, triage, or numeric thresholds.
